estimate.coverage_basis: share of the plates made that had a fully costed recipe
estimate.coverage_note: Only 37.4% of units sold have a costed recipe — the food cost % is withheld until it reaches 50%.
estimate.label: Estimated — what the units made on 10/25/26 should have cost by their recipes, at current ingredient prices; the cost counts every unit made (sold, comped and remade) and the menu price the units sold. Not a count of what was actually used.
estimate.pct_basis: theoretical cost of the plates made over the menu price of the plates sold, on the dishes that have both a recipe and a price
estimate.scope: dishes in your menu list; items the POS sold that aren't in it yet aren't counted
estimate.units_basis: the cost counts every unit made (sold, comped and remade) and the menu price the units sold
estimate.units_from: the item sales synced for the night

recoverable.basis: Only waste above each category's tolerance band counts — produce 28%, bakery 25%, beverage and pantry 20%, protein and dairy 15% of the last order. Waste inside the band is left out as expected trim and spoilage (Cavnar AI's own allowances, not a published standard) and is never counted. Summed per item from the POS-synced count and projected at 52/12 weeks a month.
recoverable.note: An opportunity projected from one week's waste — not money saved.
recoverable.projection_basis: one week extrapolated at 4.33 weeks a month — a single week, not a trend

stock.basis: Stock figures rest on counts taken 2 days ago.

variance.basis: Gap between recipe-theoretical usage and physical counts over 7 days. Reported when the gap is at least 8% of theoretical usage AND at least $15. A gap is over-portioning, prep loss or shrink — it is not counted waste.

waste.inferred_basis: inferred = what the ledger expected minus what was counted: waste, portioning or a miscount — a count can't tell them apart
